_comment: OpenShift releases this plugin is built for, one image per entry.
A single bundle cannot span releases: the console supplies react, react-router and
react-i18next as shared singletons, and those versions change between releases — most sharply
at 4.22, where the console moved React 17 -> 18. A plugin built against the wrong set loads and
then fails silently: the pod serves assets, the console skips the plugin, and every route 404s
with nothing in any server-side log.
Only 4.22 is built today. 4.23's SDK is still 4.23.0-prerelease.5, so its shared-module
contract can change before GA. Adding it is a data change here and the CI/release matrices
pick it up with no workflow edit — but it also forces the lockfile question back open, and
that is the expensive part. A second target needs a second pinned dependency tree, and
Dependabot cannot maintain two lockfiles behind one package.json: it updates package.json and
yarn.lock only, so any other lockfile goes stale and every `yarn install --immutable` fails.
So when 4.23 is added, either restore per-target lockfiles AND disable the npm ecosystem in
.github/dependabot.yml (refreshing every lockfile by hand on each bump), or keep npm updates
automated and drop back to one target. Do not leave both switched on.
'sdk' is the SDK line whose validator enforces that release's contract; 'shared' are the
versions it expects. Verify a new entry with:
A mismatch is reported as 'Console provides shared module X but plugin uses Y'.
